brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Full bases piece:1,0,0, piece:1,0,1 and piece:1,0,2 are stacked on levels 0, 1 and 2 and snapped together.
drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:0#2,0#cut sit in half bases on level 0, on either side of the column's bottom cell. The bottom cell itself, a full base, takes no drawer.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:1,0,2~hex-bin-full-div3 is a three-compartment bin in the level-2 base, with no cover over it.

finish.summary:
I built a three-storey tower with drawers on the bottom storey and an open three-compartment bin on the top. The configurator's check passes with no errors and no mesh clashes.

The tower is a column of full bases at cell (1,0), stacked on levels 0, 1 and 2. The configurator only lets a base stack on a full base, and drawers only fit on the cut face of a half base. So the two drawers are in half bases beside the column on the ground storey, at (0,0) and (2,0). The column's own bottom cell holds no drawer.

The joint is bolted and the open edges are capped with solid end caps, except one edge on the bottom storey: a cap there would run into a drawer frame, so it stays open. No cover sits over the top bin, so it stays open. The build is 49 parts, a little over the usual 40, because of the caps on all three storeys.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
